figures.public_caption: Figure 1. (a) AFM image shows single quantum dots in GaAs nanoholes after InAs growth at 3.5 × 10⁻⁷ Torr, with a 3D inset of one dot. (b) AFM image shows quantum dot pairs in nanoholes after InAs growth at 1 × 10⁻⁶ Torr, with a 3D inset of a pair. Figure 2. 3D AFM images show the initial nanohole, single quantum dot, and quantum dot pair, with corresponding profiles.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
